subject.title: [Bug]: API keys can leak in error messages when a custom provider's base URL is unreachable

question: Should this credential-exposure report be handled as a security-reviewed core provider-transport hardening change, and should the redaction boundary be shared transport error normalization rather than display-only sinks?
rationale: The source evidence shows raw exception text crossing shared provider/runtime boundaries, but security-sensitive credential handling and live repro scope should be confirmed by a maintainer before repair automation is queued.

options.title: Security-reviewed shared transport fix
options.body: Redact thrown provider/network error messages at the shared transport/error-normalization boundary and cover logs plus stream output with focused secret canary tests.

options.title: Fold into broader redaction program
options.body: Track this under the broader sensitive-data redaction work, accepting that this exact provider failure path remains open until that program lands.

options.title: Rely on existing sink redaction
options.body: Treat current logging/UI redaction as sufficient, which would leave the raw stream error-message path unresolved in source.

recommendation.title: Security-reviewed shared transport fix
recommendation.body: Redact thrown provider/network error messages at the shared transport/error-normalization boundary and cover logs plus stream output with focused secret canary tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged transport error-detail work owns the central stream error path where a shared fix would likely land first.
